video_title: Jokic’s DECLINE? // Blazers DOMINATE // Miami DISAPPOINTS | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Concerns regarding Nikola Jokic's recent performance and potential decline
quotes.excerpt: There has been a lot of talk that we may have seen the end of MVP Jokic.
quotes.quote: I wanted to see what all the fuss around Nikola Jokic has been about. There has been a lot of talk that we may have seen the end of MVP Jokic, or as our friend Bill Simmons says, Apex Jokic, the time of his career where he was unquestionably the best player in basketball, even in years he didn't win the MVP award. Those numbers have ticked down this season, so I wanted to see what was all about. I tune in, and what do I get? I get Apex Jokic. I get 32 points, I get a triple-double, I get just an outstanding performance start to finish.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Nikola Jokic's statistical regression in scoring and shooting efficiency
quotes.excerpt: His scoring is down more than four points per game from last season.
quotes.quote: You can't deny that the numbers for Nikola Jokic are not what they used to be. His scoring is down more than four points per game from last season. His field goal percentage is down seven points. His three-point percentage is down 16 points. He is shooting the low 20s from three-point range this season, and his rebounding numbers across the board have fallen off.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating Nikola Jokic's knee injury and potential impact on play
quotes.excerpt: I am wondering, has that knee gotten better? Because last year he was balling out of control.
quotes.quote: I don't want to say that we have seen the end of Jokic. It has only been eight games. But I am wondering, has that knee gotten better? Because last year he was balling out of control. It was a knee hyperextension or something along those lines at the end of December. Bone bruises are killers. They bother you for a long, long time and they take a while to heal on their own. I feel as though prior to that, he was balling outside of his mind, literally out of control, and I think when he came back he is still trying to find his footing, find his grounding.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Denver Nuggets' defensive struggles and lack of modern defensive efficiency
quotes.excerpt: They are 24th in the league in defensive rating. That is very bad.
quotes.quote: The Denver Nuggets have the sixth-best offensive rating in the NBA, that is good, at least fine. They are 24th in the league in defensive rating. That is very bad. You are not going to win a lot of games. They are not a modern offense. They are top 10 in the NBA in three-point percentage, but they are bottom five in attempts. They have a seven-attempt disadvantage against their opponents this season. Their defensive rebounding numbers have been completely off from last season. Last season they pulled down 75% of their defensive rebounds, that was in the top five. This year it is right around 68%, which puts them in the bottom third. It began with Caldwell-Pope and Bruce Brown, it continued over the years, Peyton Watson is the most recent loss that they have suffered, Tim Hardaway Jr., which just cost their bench.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential injury risks for the Denver Nuggets' starting lineup
quotes.excerpt: There is an eventual injury bug that is going to bite.
quotes.quote: What worries me the most is that with Denver, there is an eventual injury bug that is going to bite. Last season their starting five played 23 games together. Aaron Gordon historically has gotten hurt. Jamal Murray has had injury issues in the past. Cameron Johnson already missed time early this year and when he has played, he hasn't been able to buy a bucket from three either. There is some flashing red warning signs with the Denver Nuggets right now.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Portland Trail Blazers' depth and Donovan Clingan's defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: I brought up Donovan Clingan. He is averaging 12, 10, shooting over 50% from the three.
quotes.quote: I believe the Portland Trail Blazers' success is sustainable because we don't talk about the depth that they have. I brought up Donovan Clingan. He is averaging 12, 10, shooting over 50% from the three. He is shooting like 60% from the field, and he is averaging like two and a half blocks per game. That is a very good starting big right there. How he does his job and accepts his role is somewhat second to none. I think he kind of incites spirit into the team. Rob Williams just came off the bench the other day, 16 minutes, nine points, eight rebounds. There is guys that are unbelievable in their role. Drew Eubanks, either starting or stepping up, he is still a problem guard to have.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Portland Trail Blazers' defensive rebounding improvement and three-point shooting
quotes.excerpt: Portland last year was 25th in defensive rebounding. This year they are third as we tape this.
quotes.quote: Portland last year was 25th in defensive rebounding. This year they are third as we tape this. Huge jump there. I mentioned the Nuggets getting killed in terms of attempts from three-point range. Portland has a nine-attempt advantage per game from three this season. Nine. It is a big number. If you make half of them, you are in business at 12, 14, or 15 points per game. So, I give a lot of credit for how they have built out this offense and the players obviously credit for executing it.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chicago Bulls' poor performance and historically low net rating
quotes.excerpt: They have the worst net rating in the NBA, minus 17.2.
quotes.quote: I am going with Chicago. I didn't think Chicago was going to be good, I didn't think they would be Sacramento level bad. One and seven through eight games. They have the worst net rating in the NBA, minus 17.2. They have the worst three-point shooting percentage in the NBA, 27.2. Their defensive rating has fallen five points from last season. Individually, nobody seems to be playing well out there. Everyone is a lesser version of themselves. Josh Giddey is averaging less than 10 points per game this season. Josh Giddey, he was a great player last year, it looked like he was on the way up. Nikola Vucevic, another guy, 16 and a half points per game last year, right around 13 this year. His field goal percentage has dropped six points, his turnovers are up.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Miami Heat's disappointing performance and loss of team identity
quotes.excerpt: The team that I am most disappointed in, that you probably aren't shocked about, is the Miami Heat.
quotes.quote: The team that I am most disappointed in, that you probably aren't shocked about, is the Miami Heat. I think one thing I always respected so much about the Miami Heat was their culture. Everybody else, you respected the culture, you kind of bank on the culture, even in the down times. I remember having conversations you and I being like, nah, I am going to give them the benefit of the doubt. I think Spo and them are going to figure it out, but I believe when you bring over such a dominant, impactful player, you are going to take on a lot of the characteristics. I think sometimes when it comes down to it, the successor to the presence of Giannis, I feel as though has withdrawn from the Heat culture and what the Heat had on, which is great ball movement and quote-unquote defense. They have been terrible defensively this whole year.
